candidate.name: Ignacio Arsuaga
candidate.startAvailability: Target start availability: late August to early September 2026, subject to USCIS approval and EAD issuance

hero.label: Made for Sully.ai
hero.headline: I want to be the first SDR who helps Sully.ai own enterprise health systems.
hero.subheadline: Autonomous AI agents that replace entire hospital operations teams is one of the most audacious bets in healthcare right now. I want to be the person on the front lines convincing health systems to take that bet. Coming off 14 months of cold outreach at an AI startup and a summer inside a data-obsessed B2B consultancy, I know how to open doors in complex, skeptical markets.

whyCompany.title: Hospital operations is a $1T inefficiency problem finally ready to be solved by AI
whyCompany.body: Health systems are drowning in administrative overhead, staffing chaos, and disconnected workflows. Sully.ai is not building a point solution or a copilot. It is building the autonomous operating layer that replaces entire teams, which is the kind of radical value proposition that actually breaks through in enterprise sales cycles. That story sells itself to anyone who has ever watched a hospital administrator's face when you show them the cost per FTE they could eliminate.

whyCompany.title: Founding SDR means you are setting the playbook, not inheriting someone else's
whyCompany.body: Sully.ai is at the exact stage where the first enterprise SDR shapes how the company talks to health systems for the next five years. The sequences, the personas, the objection handling, the ICP definition all get built from scratch. That is not a support role. That is a co-author credit on the go-to-market story, and it is the kind of opportunity that does not come around twice.

whyCompany.title: My BDR track record at an AI startup maps directly onto what Sully.ai needs now
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai I ran cold outreach from zero and helped close 10 to 12 paying clients using HubSpot and LinkedIn sequences with no brand recognition and no inbound support. At NextAfter I spent the summer inside a B2B consultancy studying what messaging and data actually move sophisticated buyers. Selling autonomous AI to risk-averse enterprise health systems requires exactly that combination: the hunger to prospect from nothing and the analytical discipline to know why something is or is not working.

quote: I have spent the last year and a half learning how to make skeptical buyers believe in AI they have never seen before. I want to bring that into the highest-stakes version of that problem, getting a health system to hand their operations over to an autonomous agent. That pitch is hard, the market is massive, and I want to be the one making those calls.
